newsitem.title: USA: LPC - Morgan, Merrill to fund Norfolk's Conrail bid.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Morgan, Merrill to fund Norfolk's Conrail bid.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 24 (LPC) - J.P. Morgan & Co Inc and Merrill Lynch & Co Inc have agreed to syndicate a roughly $11.5 billion bank loan backing Norfolk Southern Corp's bid for Conrail Inc, banking sources said.
On Wednesday Norfolk submitted a $9 billion offer for its railroad rival.
Morgan and Merrill each would underwrite $2 billion, and they have provided a "highly confident" letter offering financing for the remainder, sources added.

The loans will be priced "more richly" than BankAmerica Corp, Bank of Nova Scotia, Chase Manhattan Bank and NationsBank's proposed $4.8 billion loan for CSX Corp's $92.50 a share acquisition bid for Conrail Inc because of the all-cash structure of Norfolk's bid, sources said.
Pricing on the proposed CSX/Conrail loan would start at 16.5 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) on drawn amounts, plus an 8.5-basis-point annual fee, according to bankers.
The CSX offer comprises about 40 percent cash and 60 percent stock.
Fees will be on offer for banks participating in the Norfolk Southern deal, a lender said.
If the roughly $11.5 billion credit is successfully syndicated, it would mark the largest merger-related bank loan completed this year, according to bankers.
